name: Deadeye Shore
summary: Deadeye Shore lies windswept along Durotar’s eastern edge, east of Drygulch Ravine. Named for Kilrogg Deadeye, the Bleeding Hollow chieftain, its barren sands are roamed by raptors, scorpids, and feral boars.

sections.title: A Shoreline of the Bleeding Hollow
sections.body: Deadeye Shore runs beneath central Durotar’s red bluffs, with sand and rocky outcrops that faintly resemble a skull missing an eye socket. The coast takes its name from Kilrogg Deadeye, the one-eyed Bleeding Hollow chieftain who fought in the First and Second Wars. No major settlement or military outpost holds the shore. It is far from peaceful: aggressive wildlife rules the sands, and Burning Blade cultists from nearby ravine hideouts have been seen prowling toward the water.

faq.q: Why is it called Deadeye Shore?
faq.answer: The shore is named for Kilrogg Deadeye, the famed Bleeding Hollow chieftain. Its natural terrain also resembles a skull missing an eye, recalling his blinded socket.
No permanent settlements occupy Deadeye Shore. Raptors, scorpids, and boars roam the coast, while fishermen and travelers sometimes pass through and may encounter hidden Burning Blade cultists.

faq.q: What threats are found around Deadeye Shore?
faq.answer: Aggressive beasts roam the coast, and Burning Blade cultists from neighboring Drygulch Ravine sometimes wander down from its rocky canyons. They ambush unwary travelers and fishermen.

angles.text: As an orc establishing a new nation in Durotar, you see a shore that honors Kilrogg Deadeye and recalls the old chieftains who shaped the Horde’s history during the wars on Azeroth.
